partners.mechanism_chain: Pyruvate Kinase L and R (HGNC:9008) —DISRUPTS→ Glycolysis (GO:0006096); Pyruvate Kinase M (HGNC:9009) —DISRUPTS→ Glycolysis (GO:0006096); Glycolysis (GO:0006096) —DECREASES→ ATP (CHEBI:15426); Glycolysis (GO:0006096) —DECREASES→ pyruvate (CHEBI:16601); phosphoenolpyruvate (CHEBI:17908) —INCREASES→ Glycolysis (GO:0006096); Glycolysis (GO:0006096) —LEADS_TO→ Hemolytic anemia (HP:0001875); Glycolysis (GO:0006096) —LEADS_TO→ Muscle weakness (HP:0001324); Glycolysis (GO:0006096) —LEADS_TO→ Exercise intolerance (HP:0009130). Mutations in either PKLR (for pyruvate kinase deficiency of red cells) or PFKM (for glycogen storage disease VII) lead to a loss-of-function of the pyruvate kinase enzyme. This enzyme is crucial for the final step of glycolysis, converting phosphoenolpyruvate to pyruvate and generating ATP. Dysfunction of this enzyme results in decreased ATP production, accumulation of upstream metabolites like phosphoenolpyruvate, and a deficit in pyruvate. The reduced ATP production particularly affects high-energy demand tissues like red blood cells (leading to hemolytic anemia) and muscles (leading to muscle weakness and exercise intolerance).

falsification.text: The identification of a pathogenic variant in PKLR or PFKM with a significantly high allele frequency (>1%) in the gnomAD database for the relevant population would cast doubt on the causal role of these genes for the respective diseases, thereby falsifying this hypothesis. raw.translational: Understanding the shared reliance on glycolysis and ATP production between pyruvate kinase deficiency of red cells and glycogen storage disease VII could inform therapeutic strategies. For instance, interventions aimed at improving glycolytic flux or ATP generation, or mitigating the downstream consequences of ATP depletion in affected tissues, might have broader applicability across both conditions.
